newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet approves postal liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet approves postal liberalisation.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Wednesday gave the green light for plans to liberalise Germany's postal services industry beginning in January and culminating in full competition in the year 2002.

A draft bill will now be sent to parliament and if passed, pave the way for private firms such as United Parcel Service and Federal Express of the United States to win a greater share of the market from nopoly Deutsche Post AG.

Under the draft legislation, the post office monopoly will be restricted to delivering letters weighing up to 100 grams. But even this thread of a centuries-old postal monopoly would be cut in 2002 when all postal services are to be deregulated.
The main opposition Social Democrats (SPD) warned that if the bill became law, it would endanger jobs at the post office and comprehensive postal services to the broad public.
SPD postal expert Hans-Martin Bury urged the government to grant the post office an indefinite monopoly on delivery of letters and direct mail advertising under 100 grams.
Otherwise, he said, the post office would not be able to afford to maintain pensions for thousands of civil servant employees.
